rationale: A unanimous Court is most likely to issue a Roberts opinion reaffirming Geders’ categorical rule that overnight consultation bans (even if topic-limited) violate the Sixth Amendment, while reading Perry as limited to very brief mid-testimony breaks. Some separate concurrences are plausible to emphasize original meaning (Thomas/Gorsuch), practical trial-management and anti-coaching alternatives (Alito/Kavanaugh/Barrett), or defendant-protective concerns about chilling privileged communications (Sotomayor/Jackson).
